name: The Honking Deep (eldritch goose boss)
scale_note: Boss scale against the 1.80 m reference human: about 6.7 m to the twig tips of the main head's dead maple crown (crown of the head about 5.15 m, held high like a standing goose's), 8.5 m across from finger-claw to finger-claw. Faces -Y, +Z up, origin on the ground between the feet. All design numbers below are metres in that frame.
budget_note: Hero asset: every tooth, rib, hackle and feather is real geometry; surface detail (barbs, hide, bark, grime, blood, the brand) is baked texture.

materials.name: PlumageEdge
materials.notes: ashen feather-edge bars on the flanks

materials.name: MawRed
materials.notes: dried blood: the heads' mouths and tongues, the soaked breast feathers

materials.notes: yellowed bone: teeth, spines, ribs, claws, finger bones

materials.notes: one small wet sunken eye a side per head, no glow

materials.name: DeadBark

body_rings.note: [y, z_centre, half_width, half_height] from breast to tail tip; side profile traced off a photo of a standing Canada goose (body length scaled to 3.3 m): the body tilts down from chest to tail and the belly is deepest just behind the legs

side_neck.note: the +X neck; the -X one is its mirror

wing.note: the +X wing, raised in a threat display; the -X one is its mirror

v2.note: version 2 (Models #17, #18): read only by goose_design.build_parts(version=2) and build_goose.py --v2; version 1 ignores this block

main_neck.note: one root rising from the chest that becomes the main neck; the side necks branch off its top at about 3.05 m. From path[2] up it is version 1's main neck, so the main head stays where it was

side_neck.note: the +X neck, starting inside the root's top; from path[2] up it is version 1's side neck, so the side heads stay where they were

skin.note: the soft parts melted into one closed skin: a voxel remesh, then smoothing only within join_width_m of where two soft parts meet, then a decimate down to triangle_cap. Colour and pattern are carried over from the nearest version 1 style surface until Models #20 re-bakes them

build: Body: lofted ellipse rings, about 3.3 m long, 1.76 m wide, 1.46 m deep, lowest point 1.10 m just behind the legs; the body tilts down from chest to tail like a standing goose's; soot-brown back, ashen bars on the flanks, grimy breast (straight seam at y = -0.42 m), dirty-bone belly and undertail; five bare ribs break through each flank.

Necks: one main neck rising straight out of the chest to 4.95 m, head held high and level like a standing goose's, radius 0.50 m where it rises out of the chest, tapering to 0.165 m; two side necks rising upright to +/-1.15 m and 4.05 m, radius 0.26 to 0.13 m. All black, a ridge of 13 bone spines down the back of the main neck.

Heads: goose heads crowned with dead bare maple branches (two gnarled limbs 0.85 m long, spread sideways like antlers and forking three times, a few rotting leaves still hanging), the white chinstrap, one small sunken dark eye a side, beaks gaping (42 deg main, 58 deg side) with rows of teeth on both mandibles and a spiked tongue. Side heads at 0.74 scale.

Wings: raised and spread, 8.5 m across including the bare finger bones, arm 0.17 m to 0.04 m thick; 10 badly ragged primaries 1.45 to 1.05 m, 12 secondaries, 5 tertials, two covert rows; two finger bones 1.25 m long with claws break out past the primaries.
Legs: black, hip 1.55 m to ankle; three webbed toes 0.48 m long spread 32 deg, bone claws, a small back toe.
Tail: nine ragged black feathers 0.9 m long in a cupped fan over 80 deg, outer feathers banked and drooping so the fan reads from the side.
Spines: a bone ridge along the back and down the main neck.

Dead maple: no leaves left anywhere, only bare dead branches; a maple leaf about 0.7 m across branded into the centre of the breast, painted into the texture as a charred scar with an ember-red raised rim; below it three rows of thin ragged breast feathers (15, 16, 17) 0.4 to 0.85 m long hanging down like a matted bib, splayed unevenly and soaked in dried blood from halfway or higher.
style: Canadian Bloodborne-style beast horror: a goose gone feral in a dead maple wood. Soot, ash, grimy bone, dried blood; starved and ragged; no emissive materials.

albedo_gain.note: multipliers on each palette colour in the bake only, so the lit render reads at the concept sheet's flat tones (measured: breast rendered 0.67x, wings 0.8x, black 1.8x the concept)

rig.note: built by art/goose/build_rig.py from the design numbers above; goose_rigged.blend
rig.naming: goose's own point of view (Blender convention): it faces -Y, so .L / _L is +X (its left) and .R / _R is -X. goose_design tags its parts the other way round; build_rig.py's BONE_SIDE table maps across.
bones: per side (.L/.R): wing_shoulder, wing_upper, wing_fore, wing_hand, wing_finger_1..4, leg_thigh, leg_shin, leg_tarsus, leg_toes
rig.weighting: computed per part by name, not Blender bone-heat: soft parts blend neighbouring bones along their chain by arc length with a smoothstep; feathers, hackles, ribs and spines take the blend at their root vertex; teeth, beaks, jaws, tongues, eyes, crown branches, claws, toes and scutes are 100% on one bone; finger bones split at the knuckle. Weights sum to 1, at most 3 bones per vertex.
